raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies reversible, assembled organizers and checks order slips, but median time is 11 minutes and only seven of ten participants succeeded unaided. Five partition complaints suggest contents errors without establishing incidence or cause. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting an account that assembly is uniformly too slow; mixed-batch delays could reflect switching or complexity. Width overlap in D2-O5 limits a width-only explanation of insertion retries. No damage claims provisionally support retaining current packaging. These synthetic observations do not establish proposed mechanisms.

openings.claim: Selecting and verifying an entire order kit before insertion may reduce selection interruptions and contents errors while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Replace interleaved picking with reusable staging and an order-specific checklist for partition types, quantities and exterior color.
openings.prediction: Within worker and layout, staging should reduce selection/checking time or errors. Including all preparation labor may erase apparent savings.
openings.probe: Counterbalance 12 sample builds: each worker builds each layout once per workflow. Time selection, insertion, checking, packing and kit preparation separately; independently inspect contents. Use reusable spare-board aids. Confirm actual costs and available time before adoption within the fixed delivery schedule; retain ordered counts, colors, footprint, capacity and removable joints.
assumptions: Reusable aids fit the bench and budget caps.
Sample work fits available time; twelve builds provide exploratory evidence only.

openings.claim: Do short-partition difficulties persist with verified contents and a diagram explicitly depicting the ordered layout and short-partition position?
openings.delta: Distinguish location uncertainty from insertion difficulty using separate identification and insertion observations.
openings.prediction: Improved identification without improved insertion supports a guidance limitation alongside a separate insertion problem. Persistent identification errors weaken this diagram hypothesis.
openings.probe: Use ten participants and verified samples in the usual shipping state; assign five the current diagram and five an ordered-layout sketch on the existing slip, balancing layout and prior exposure. Record unaided completion, location errors and insertion retries. Include sketch labor and confirm cost caps. Subsequently verify all success targets across the 60-order pilot.
assumptions: Sketches accurately represent selected arrangements and fit existing slips without added material cost.
Ten participants cannot establish pilot success rates.

raw.assessment: Two unvalidated conversions. The observations establish selection, interpretation and insertion difficulties, but not their causes. Neither alternative yet demonstrates the pilot targets or feasibility within the fixed delivery date and cost caps.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: turn configuration differences into a visual completeness signal using reusable order-specific bench stencils with one outlined position per required component. A missing or mismatched part leaves a visible discrepancy; corresponding position labels on the existing customer diagram guide placement.
openings.delta: Uses variation and selection mistakes to generate checking information. Trial packing the checked components unassembled could remove workshop insertion time while retaining customer rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary order-slip checks, stencils detect more deliberately seeded missing or incorrect parts; matched customer labels reduce questions about short partitions.
openings.probe: Counterbalance stencil and ordinary checking trials across workers and layouts; separately time selection, checking and packing. Record seeded-error detection. Test labeled kits with the ten participants, then evaluate all success measures in the 60-unit pilot if feasible.
assumptions: Failure boundary: visually identical but functionally different parts evade outlines unless separately marked.
Customer assembly effort must remain compatible with the unaided-success target.
Template preparation, labeling and any packing changes must meet both cost caps and the fixed date; preserve ordered count, exterior color, footprint and capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a compliant, removable tongue cut into the insertion edge converts slot resistance into elastic deflection and restoring force that seats and retains the partition.
openings.delta: Replaces a rigid insertion interface with controlled compliance; dimensional overlap does not establish that interference caused the observed retries.
openings.prediction: Matched compliant samples require fewer retries and lower peak insertion force while retaining loaded stability and repeated removability.
openings.probe: Use six modified and six unchanged samples, holding board and slot dimensions comparable. Measure force, retries, loaded stability and repeated rearrangement damage; cost and time any template change before adoption.
assumptions: Failure boundary: board creasing, tearing or creep dissipates restoring force; orientation errors may receive no benefit.
Preserve footprint, stationery capacity, selected counts and exterior colors without permanent bonds; reject adoption if costs or preparation threaten the fixed delivery date.

openings.claim: Stage/check complete kits before full assembly.
openings.probe: Counterbalance 12 builds across workers/layouts/workflows; time every stage; independently inspect contents.
openings.uncertainty: Switching versus complexity unresolved; bench space unverified.

openings.claim: Depict ordered layout and short-partition position.
openings.probe: Ten participants, five per diagram; balance layout/exposure; verified contents, usual shipping state; record completion, location errors, retries and sketch labor.

openings.claim: Outlines expose incomplete kits; matching labels guide placement; unassembled packing shifts insertion to customers.
openings.probe: Counterbalance stencil/ordinary checks across workers/layouts; time preparation and stages; test labeled kits with ten participants.
openings.uncertainty: Lookalike mismatches need marking; customer burden and packaging changes.

openings.claim: Removable compliant tongues convert resistance into seating/retention force.
openings.discriminator: Lower force/retries with stable, reusable joints.
openings.probe: Compare six modified/six unchanged samples, comparable board/slots; measure force, retries, loaded stability, rearrangement damage, template cost/time.
openings.uncertainty: Interference unproven; orientation errors, tearing, creasing and creep.

post_distill.decision: Exploratory only; coordinate within 15 samples, ten participants and available time. Gate adoption on 30x20 cm footprint, same capacity, selected counts/colors, removable partitions, <=500 initial/<=0.40 recurring material costs and fixed delivery. Count all labor. Verify 60-order targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided. Synthetic observations establish no mechanism.
